_: Phrase -> Special Orders picker code map for the migrated SO/PO backfill.
_field: The picker reads variants.specials (SpecialOrders.tsx:91). custom_specials is a DERIVED OUTPUT of mfg-pricing-recompute (mfg-pricing-recompute.ts:283/604) and is overwritten on the first UI edit (mfg-sales-orders.ts:8234), so it is NOT a place to store an operator choice.
_phrases: The phrase side is what the parsers actually emit: parseSofa's special-order sweep (parse-sofa.mjs:45-60, pinned in backend/tests/parseSofaGrammar.test.ts:117-160) and parse-bedframe's specials block (parse-bedframe.mjs:134-160).
_matching: Each phrase is normalised to ' words separated by single spaces ' (lower case, every non [a-z0-9] run -> space, wrapped in spaces) before `yes`/`no` are tested. `no` is a veto and runs first. Codes are resolved against the LIVE scm.special_addons read; a family whose code is not live is reported MISSING and its phrases fall through to UNMAPPED. Never invent a code.
_owner: Owner rulings 2026-08-10 are recorded per family in `why`, and the deliberate non-mappings are in `excluded` (they are NOT gaps).

parseSofa emits 'wooden arm' (parse-sofa.mjs:100) and the raw slip wording. Fabric colour codes ending in WOOD ('CH141-4 WOOD') never reach here — parseSofa drops them as COLOUR_LIKE (parseSofaGrammar.test.ts:152).

'notch' is the stitched dimple in a seat cushion; these slips all say do not put one there. Vetoed when the slip also says plain, which is the separate code below. The three conditions are INDEPENDENT lookaheads, mirroring lib/sofa-special-map.mjs's three separate tests, and a stitch word satisfies the seat-part condition on its own — the stitching IS the cushion detail. The earlier ordered `a.*b.*c` form demanded three DISTINCT tokens in sequence and so missed 'NO HOLES ON STICHING' and 'NO STICHING', two real slip phrases (ac-outstanding-so), while the lib matched them: one owner ruling, two copies, drifted.

_cushionSwap: Owner: backrest and back cushion are the same word, and the picker carries exactly one code per model number, so both wordings route to the model's code. Applies only when the phrase says back rest / back cushion. When the phrase names two model numbers ('9058 sofa backrest change 9028') the LAST one is the model being changed TO. 5537/5540 are their own products and are matched by the families above, which run first. Codes follow the owner's own spelling, which is deliberately inconsistent (fix-sofa-special-addon-names.mjs) — do not tidy it.
